title: pull_request_target workflows: no PR checkout, minimal token, serialized per PR
answers: can stack nudge check out the PR branch
why is the nudge workflow concurrency queued
safe way to comment on fork PRs from a workflow
body:
Invariant: the Stack Nudge workflow runs on `pull_request_target` but does not check out the repository or PR code. It only runs inline bash and `gh` against the PR number and repo.
Enforced in: .github/workflows/stack-nudge.yml (no checkout step; top-level `permissions: {}`; job-level `permissions: pull-requests: write`; `GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` on the Nudge step).
What breaks if skipped: checking out PR head under `pull_request_target` runs untrusted PR code with a write-scoped token and repository secrets.
Ordering: `concurrency` is keyed per PR number, with `cancel-in-progress: false` and `queue: max`, so runs for successive edits are queued and not cancelled. This keeps the dedupe check and the comment post from racing on the same PR.
applies: Any new or edited workflow triggered by pull_request_target in this repository.
says: Ensure automated PR reminder comments on external forks cannot execute untrusted contributor code.
Stack nudge bot posts overlapping duplicate comments when an author pushes several commits quickly.
Queue automated stack suggestions sequentially per pull request instead of cancelling intermediate updates.
Limit automated bot permissions so pull request nudges only have write access for comments.
search: Workflows triggered by pull_request_target, such as .github/workflows/stack-nudge.yml, must not check out the repository or PR head code to avoid executing untrusted code with write permissions. The workflow configures top-level permissions: {}, job-level permissions: pull-requests: write, and passes GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} to an inline bash and gh step. Concurrency is keyed per PR number with cancel-in-progress: false and queue: max so runs for successive edits queue without racing.
